options.content:
Every panel is **per node** — that is the point since Stage 3. `chat_ws_connections_open` summed across the cluster hides the case that matters: 500 sockets on one node and 0 on the other.

When a number here looks wrong, open the same moment in [Jaeger](http://localhost:16686). Metrics say *something is slow*; a trace says *which step*.

panels.title: Requests per second, by node
panels.description: Both nodes should carry roughly the same load. A node at zero is a node nginx has taken out — check /readyz.

panels.title: Request latency p99, by route
panels.description: The send path should sit near 10ms. Everything after the 201 happens on the relay's own time and is not in here — that part is only visible on a trace.

panels.title: Outbox pending
panels.description: Rows written and not yet published. Zero at rest. It climbs the moment NATS goes away and drains when it returns — nothing is lost, only late.

panels.title: Outbox lag
panels.description: How long the oldest waiting row has waited. This is the number the outbox.publish span shows for one message; here it is the whole queue.

panels.title: Relay leader
panels.description: Exactly one node must be 1. Two would publish seq 5 before seq 4 and throw away Stage 4; zero means nothing is draining the outbox.

panels.title: Presence circuit breaker
panels.description: 1 means a node has stopped calling presenced. Watch the two nodes differ: a node nobody is asking learns nothing, and its breaker stays closed through the whole outage.
